reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge: two blocking issues.*

1. *Whole-string validation is bypassable* — `src/validate.js:1–4`
   The regex matches any valid substring, so `Hello`, `a/b`, `../admin`, `hello world`, and `"hello\n"` all pass and produce page URLs. Encoding in `pagePath` doesn’t enforce the slug rules.
   *Fix:* require the entire string to contain only `[a-z0-9-]`. Include trailing-newline rejection—JavaScript’s `$` anchor alone can match before a final newline.

2. *Reserved slugs aren’t enforced* — `src/route.js:4–5`
   `pagePath` never calls `isReserved`, so all four reserved values (`new`, `edit`, `admin`, `api`) produce page URLs despite the documented restriction.
   *Fix:* reject reserved names before returning a path, and add route-level tests covering all four.

All 4 existing tests pass, but `test/validate.test.js` covers only valid strings, a number, and the empty string; `test/reserved.test.js` checks the helper without exercising `pagePath`. I reproduced both failures directly.

No code changed.
